answer: Agents in a decentralized economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to wander through a dynamic sequence of real-time verification puzzles linked to fluctuating market data, generating a continuous tide of unique proofs that must be submitted within tight windows. This forces attackers to expend substantial compute and latency costs for every fake identity, while a lotus of staked tokens acts as collateral that is burned if coordinated sybil patterns are detected by peer monitors, making mass impersonation economically prohibitive.
